finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unvalidated `q` query parameter is interpolated into a SQL string literal via an f-string and executed, letting an unauthenticated attacker alter the query and read arbitrary database content (e.g. sqlite_master and other tables) via UNION SELECT.
finding.source: app.py:11 — request.args.get("q", "") (remote HTTP query parameter, attacker-controlled, no authentication required)
finding.sink: app.py:12 — db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'"), result returned by jsonify at app.py:13

trace.note: term taken verbatim from request.args 'q'; default empty string; no type, length, or character validation
term concatenated into SQL text inside a single-quoted LIKE literal; no placeholder; executed with db.execute
all fetched rows returned to caller as JSON, so injected UNION results are directly visible

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no escaping or quote-doubling, no allowlist, no parameter binding (contrast /product line 18 and /by-owner line 25, which use ? placeholders), no authentication/authorization, no input length limit. The identifier-allowlist decoy (case 25) does not apply because input is a string-literal value, not an identifier. sqlite3 execute() runs a single statement so stacked queries are not possible, but UNION-based read injection is. Not executed: shop.db is absent, so this is from code reading.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:11 takes `q` verbatim with a default of "", app.py:12 interpolates it into a single-quoted LIKE literal via f-string and calls db.execute with no placeholder, and app.py:13 returns all rows via jsonify. The only parameterized queries are at app.py:18 and app.py:25, which are not on this path. The route at app.py:9 has no authentication or authorization decorator, and no before_request hook appears in app.py.
verdict.reason: The `/search` route at app.py:9-13 is reachable anonymously, and `term` from `request.args.get("q")` (app.py:11) is concatenated unescaped into the SQL string at app.py:12 and its rows are returned to the caller at app.py:13, so a UNION SELECT payload can read arbitrary tables such as sqlite_master.
